title: BASKET OF INVESTMENTS
mv: Cast your bread upon the waters, For you will find it after many days.
mvp: “Cast your bread upon the waters, For you will find it after many days.” Ecclesiastes 11:1 (NKJV)
assignment: List five (5) ways you can invest your finances more wisely and biblically (2X5=10 marks).

b.x: Life is full of opportunities and risks. The Bible teaches us the wisdom of planning and diversifying (Ecclesiastes 11:1-2). Just as farmers sow in different fields, wise people do not put all their resources in one place. For today’s youths, especially in various parts of the world, where the economy is unstable, it is important to learn how to create a “basket of investments.”

A basket of investments means managing multiple streams of income: diversifying your income and resources across different opportunities so that if one fails, others can sustain you (Ecclesiastes 11:2). This protects against total loss and increases the chances of long-term success. In practical terms, you do not keep all your money in one investment portfolio, or one business, or one type of investment. Instead, you spread it across safe, moderate, and growth-driven opportunities and also based on your risk capacity.
Here are some practical Investment opportunities that youths can explore:

i: Savings and Fixed Deposits: This comes with low risk and steady returns. Helps build financial discipline (Proverbs 21:20).
Treasury Bills and Government Bonds: This is risk-free because they are backed by the government. Good for capital preservation and steady income.

Agriculture and Agro-Business: Farming (arable crop production, vegetables, etc.), poultry, fishery, or agro-tech platforms. Nigeria’s economy is largely agricultural, with a steady demand for food. In Genesis 26:12 - Isaac sowed in the land and reaped a hundredfold.
Real Estate: Buying land, renting property, and short-let apartments. Land hardly depreciates, especially in growing cities.

Stocks and Mutual Funds: Investing in Stocks and Mutual funds allows you to pool money with others for professional management. Think of Joseph storing grain in abundance in Genesis 41; this is a long-term wealth creation strategy.
Entrepreneurship/Small Business: Starting a side hustle or gig (e.g., fashion, tech-services, digital marketing, and logistics) builds skills, creates jobs, and provides multiple streams of income.
Digital Investments: Tech start-ups, online businesses, and carefully chosen Fintech platforms. Be cautious: avoid scams and Ponzi schemes (Proverbs 28:20).

b.x: Investments follow some basic guiding principles:

i: Start with God: Pray for direction and seek Divine wisdom (Proverbs 3:5-6, James 1:5).
Start early: The earlier you start, the more time your investment has to grow. (Ecclesiastes 11:4).
Start small but be consistent: Faithful little steps compound into much. (Proverbs 4:25).
Diversify: Do not put all your eggs in one basket. Diversification helps protect against uncertainty.
Avoid greed and shortcuts: Many youths lose money to Ponzi schemes due to greed and impatience. (Proverbs 13:11).
Engage the services of financial experts where necessary (Proverbs 15:22).

b.x: God has given us wisdom and resources to prosper. Just as a farmer plants in many fields, so must we build a sustainable basket of investments.
